must_remember: Beta-minus decay involves the conversion of a neutron into a proton: $n \rightarrow p + e^- + \bar{\nu}_e$.
Beta-plus decay requires the parent neutral atom mass to exceed the daughter atom mass by at least $2m_e c^2$.
Electron capture is a competing process where an inner-shell electron is captured by the nucleus: $p + e^- \rightarrow n + \nu_e$.
Unlike alpha decay, beta decay exhibits a continuous energy spectrum due to the sharing of decay energy $Q$ with a neutrino or antineutrino.
Wolfgang Pauli postulated the neutrino to conserve energy, momentum, and angular momentum (spin $1/2$) in beta decay.
Fermi's Golden Rule governs the transition rate of beta decay, combining the weak interaction matrix element and density of final states.

glossary.meaning: A radioactive decay process in which an unstable neutron-rich nucleus emits an electron and an antineutrino.
A radioactive decay process in which a proton-rich nucleus emits a positron and a neutrino.
A process where a nucleus absorbs an inner-shell orbital electron, converting a proton into a neutron and emitting a neutrino.
A linearization plot of $K(E) = \sqrt{\frac{N(E)}{F(Z, E) p E}} \propto (Q - E)$ used to analyze beta spectra and determine endpoint energy.
Expression giving the transition rate per unit time: $\lambda = \frac{2\pi}{\hbar} |M_{if}|^2 \rho(E_f)$.
